title: T1566 - Phishing
summary: Adversaries send phishing messages to gain initial access to victim systems. Phishing can be untargeted mass mailing or highly tailored spearphishing.
mitigation: Enforce strict SPF, DKIM, and DMARC policies (p=reject). Deploy multi-factor authentication resilient to phishing (FIDO2/WebAuthn). Implement automated link analysis and quarantine pipelines.
d3fend_mapping: D3-EAA (Email Authentication Analysis), D3-MTA (Mail Transfer Agent Filtering)

title: T1566.001 - Spearphishing Attachment
summary: Adversaries attach weaponized files (e.g. ISO disk images, VBS scripts, HTA applications, password-protected archives) designed to execute code upon opening.
indicators: Encrypted ZIP with password in email body
mitigation: Block dangerous executable and script attachments at the secure email gateway. Unpack containers (.iso, .vhd, .zip) and inspect child payloads in air-gapped sandboxes.
d3fend_mapping: D3-FA (File Content Analysis), D3-EBE (Executable Binary Extraction)

title: T1566.002 - Spearphishing Link
summary: Adversaries send emails containing hyperlinks that direct victims to credential harvesting portals, reverse-proxy phishing kits (e.g. Evilginx), or drive-by malware downloads.
mitigation: Static link syntax verification without making live network requests. Block direct IP URLs, Punycode homographs, and internal cloud metadata requests. Enforce FIDO2 WebAuthn keys.
d3fend_mapping: D3-URLA (URL Analysis), D3-DNSA (DNS Domain Reputation Analysis)

title: T1586.002 - Compromised Email Account
summary: Adversaries compromise legitimate email accounts (via credential stuffing, session hijacking, or password reuse) and use them to send trusted phishing and BEC requests to vendors, partners, and colleagues.
indicators: Valid SPF/DKIM/DMARC pass from known vendor domain
Mismatched Reply-To header pointing to external domain
New bank account or remittance routing request
Evasion keywords like 'do not call me'
mitigation: Mandatory out-of-band telephone verification for financial record modifications. Implement anomalous mailbox behavior alerting (impossible travel, new forwarding rules).
d3fend_mapping: D3-EAA (Email Authentication Analysis), D3-UDBA (User & Domain Behavioral Analytics)

title: T1534 - Internal Spearphishing
summary: Adversaries use a compromised internal corporate email account to send spearphishing emails to other employees within the same organization to escalate privileges or expand access.
indicators: Internal From header matching corporate domain
Requesting HR/payroll updates or executive approval
Absence of internal authentication results or strange relay hops
mitigation: Inspect internal-to-internal email traffic with the same rigor as perimeter mail. Require step-up MFA for sensitive actions. Monitor anomalous internal email volume spikes.
